answer.answer: Chevron acquired Hess Corporation on July 18, 2025, and the aggregate purchase price was approximately $48 billion, including 15.38 million shares of Hess common stock bought in open market transactions in the first quarter of 2025 and 301.25 million shares of Chevron common stock issued as closing consideration in July [1]. The company assumed debt with an aggregate outstanding principal value of $8.8 billion, and the shares issued represented approximately 15 percent of Chevron common stock outstanding immediately after closing [1]. The acquisition was accounted for as a business combination under ASC 805, and as a result there was no goodwill or bargain purchase recognized [1]. Chevron states that the success of the acquisition will depend on its ability to realize anticipated benefits, including run-rate cost synergies and estimated five-year production and free cash flow growth rates [2]. Hess's legacy reserves staff and processes continued to be relied upon for reserves review, and the legacy Hess proved reserves represent approximately 13 percent of Chevron's total proved reserves [3].
